content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: hosted-runtime kv-heap surge detected — multiple OOMs on inference nodes in us-east1. Paging eng-sre and eng-runtime. thread_ts=5291234567

maya: I’m seeing a rapid kv_cache size growth on runtime-*-pool-3, almost linear with a few long prompts hitting 80k+ tokens. memory per-session jumping to 45GB then OOM.

loren: logs show repeated prefetch spikes from continuous-batching controller during decode. stack traces point at kvmap.insert loop. snippet:
```
E 12:03:21 kvmap.cpp:478 Insert failed: mem_alloc 2147483648 -> abort
WARN continuous_batcher: prefetch_window=65536 requests=312 active_sessions=98
```

aj: 👍 on the logs. Query: is this a single model or multi-model? telemetry says majority for model=redwood-open-30b, some routes pinned to long-context mode.

sre-oncall: on it, grabbing access. first priority: stop further OOMs to avoid cascade. Recommended immediate mitigations?

runtime-lead: we can flip prefetch throttle to conservative mode (prefetch.max_window=8192) and reduce continuous_batcher.max_batch_tokens from 65536 -> 16384. That should cap memory amplification. Want to patch config and restart controller.

maya: please also push session-prefix-cap to 64k tokens for hosted runtime; some clients send huge system prompts repeatedly.

loren: adding short-term eviction policy: evict keys not accessed in last 20s from kv-cache for hosts with >70% used. That may bring memory down quickly.

aj: can we do a non-disruptive toggle? ops-bot supports dynamic flags for prefetch and batcher.

ops-bot: run `/flag set continuous_batcher.prefetch_mode conservative --env=prod --hosts=us-east1` will rollout 10% -> 100% over 2 min.

ops-bot: command queued, applying.

ops-bot: applied to 10% of hosts.

sre-oncall: watching metrics. CPU and latency spikes expected during rollout, but better than OOM.

cs-esc: heads up — CS:customer-team-1 reported API 502s starting ~12:02 UTC, likely related. We have a support incident open.

runtime-lead: also plan B: fallback routing to smaller model variant (redwood-open-13b-ctx) for routes with >60s latency or >32k token prefixes. We can enable fallback using routing policy: latency-first.

maya: doing a quick grep across traces, list of affected session ids attached to thread (omitted) — a handful heavy sessions from a vector-store ingestion job.

loren: evictions kicking in on hosts where flag applied, memory trending down from 92% -> 64% on first wave.

aj: ok, once conservative prefetch is at 50% and eviction is active, let's pause all new long-context sessions via gateway rule: `block if session_prefix_tokens > 65536` with 503 for new ones.

ops-bot: gateway rule applied to edge-us-east1.

cs-esc: customer-team-1 reports degraded but recovering. They still see some 5xx for in-progress sessions, but new requests are being throttled.

sre-oncall: updating incident channel and status page: setting status->investigating -> partial-mitigation

runtime-lead: we should also hotfix continuous_batcher to prevent exponential prefetch loops. Quick patch: ensure prefetch depth scales sublinearly with session prefix length. I’ll open PR and cherry-pick to hotfix branch.

aj: timeline? we need hotfix merged and rollout to prod in next 45m if stability not regained.

loren: quick sanity check: do we have any eviction-induced correctness regressions risk? some models rely on older KV entries for beam search. Eviction depth 20s should be safe, we can raise to 60s if needed.

maya: monitoring hallucination/regression metrics for affected flows. so far no spike in error-rate aside from 502s.

ops-bot: conservative prefetch flag at 100% in us-east1.

sre-oncall: memory across pool has stabilized ~62-68%. No new OOMs in last 6 minutes.

cs-esc: update for customers: CS sent initial notice to the three impacted accounts, offering timeline and workaround (restarting sessions or using the smaller model). We’re coordinating follow-ups.

runtime-lead: PR opened: gh/infra/continuous-batcher#429 hotfix -> backport to prod. includes guard `max_prefetch = min(max_prefetch, 16384)` and a safety circuit to abort prefetch loop if observed growth > 20% in 5s.

aj: thumbs. After hotfix, we should run canary on 5 hosts for 10m, verify no perf cliffs, then roll.

loren: running the canary now.

ops-bot: canary started on hosts: runtime-3a, runtime-3b, runtime-3c

sre-oncall: will handoff watch to runtime-lead in 30m. Add pager escalation if memory rises >75% again.

cs-esc: customer-team-2 pinged, they use session replay ingestion; gave them temporary suggestion to chunk prompts and backoff prefetch. They’ll try now.

aj: quick note: we should add a rate-limit at API layer for total token window per session to prevent this class. filing a short RFC after incident.

maya: agreed — tracking as follow-up: ENG-INC-1223 (limit session window + better telemetry on session token delta).

loren: canary looks clean for 8m, memory stable, no new OOMs.

runtime-lead: rolling hotfix to remaining hosts in 3 waves.

ops-bot: rollout wave 1 -> 33% done, wave 2 -> 66% done, wave 3 -> 100% done.

sre-oncall: full rollout completed. Observed a transient latency increase (~40ms p95) but stable.

cs-esc: CS confirms customers seeing normal behavior now; closing support incidents pending follow-up comms.

aj: incident summary for postmortem: root cause: continuous-batcher prefetch scaling incorrectly with session prefix length, combined with rising longprompt workload and no session token caps. Contributing: lack of early eviction policy and insufficient routing fallback.

maya: mitigation timeline: prefetch conservative flag + eviction + gateway token cap at 12:06-12:12; hotfix PR merged and rolled 12:30-12:55; full stabilization by 13:05 UTC.

runtime-lead: next steps: (1) backport hotfix to dedicated and private stacks, (2) add session-token cap at gateway and runtime, (3) add telemetry alert for kv-cache growth > 25%/min, (4) run load tests with longprompt scenarios.

loren: assigning follow-ups on GH: ENG-1234 (hotfix backport), ENG-1235 (gateway token cap), ENG-1236 (kv-growth alert), ENG-1237 (longprompt load tests).

sre-oncall: handing off monitoring to oncall-next. I’ll add summary to incident-runbook and mark this thread as recovery-phase.

aj: closing note — nice quick coordination, ops-bot flags saved us from repeat OOMs. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: incident update: mitigated -> monitoring. last_message_ts=5291234687
